text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthHow Our Skin Reveals the Link Between Insomnia and FearIt’s an exhausting cycleJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on October 16, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEvery Dune fan knows fear is the mind killer, but it might also be the sleep killer. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayFear and sleep share a close bond, according to research, with insomnia increasing the risk of developing fear and anxiety disorders and fear and anxiety disorders robbing people of a good night’s sleep. Additionally, insomniacs live in a state of chronic hyperarousal, with their fight-or-flight systems humming away in the background even when there’s no threat. Simply put, it’s an exhausting cycle. Now a new study published in PLOS Mental Health might give researchers a better way to understand the relationship between fear and sleep. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
